stem: Five people Kiran, Lata, Manish, Nisha, and Prem sit in a row at positions 1 to 5. Prem is at position 1. Manish is at position 5. Lata sits immediately to the left of Nisha. Kiran is not at position 2. Who sits at position 4?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Prem=1, Manish=5. Lata-Nisha block (L immediately left of N) can sit at (2,3) or (3,4). If at (3,4): Kiran goes to position 2, violating Kiran-not-at-2. If at (2,3): Kiran goes to position 4. Valid. Arrangement: Prem(1) Lata(2) Nisha(3) Kiran(4) Manish(5). Position 4 = Kiran.
Lata is at position 2 (left end of the LN block). Placing Lata at position 4 would require Nisha at position 5, but Manish is fixed at position 5. This option omits the Manish-at-5 constraint.
Manish is explicitly placed at position 5, not position 4. Selecting Manish at position 4 misreads the fixed placement clue.

Placing Nisha at position 4 forces Lata at position 3 (LN block at 3,4) and Kiran at position 2. But Kiran is not at position 2, which is violated. This results from reversing the Kiran-not-at-2 constraint or not applying it.

explanation: Prem=1 and Manish=5 are fixed. The Lata-Nisha block (Lata immediately left of Nisha) occupies two consecutive positions from {2,3,4}. The block can sit at (2,3) or (3,4). If the block is at (3,4): Kiran is the only remaining person and goes to position 2 - but Kiran must not be at position 2, so this is invalid. The block must be at (2,3): Lata=2, Nisha=3, Kiran=4. Position 4 is Kiran.

explanation_sections.punchline: The Kiran-not-at-2 constraint eliminates the (3,4) placement of the Lata-Nisha block, uniquely placing Kiran at position 4.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: anchor Prem(1) and Manish(5). Slide the LN block through its two candidate positions in {2,3,4}. Apply the Kiran-not-at-2 constraint to reject one placement. Read position 4 from the surviving arrangement.
explanation_sections.lesson: When an adjacent-pair block has two candidate positions, a negative constraint on the leftover person resolves the ambiguity in one step.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 seconds. Two anchors, two block positions, one negative check, done.
